The unshadowed builtin repr receives an ordinary function object and returns its representation; it does not call f or hand f to a callback. Therefore subprocess.run is unreachable and the transcript should produce no findings. The required preamble is import subprocess so f's deferred body visibly contains a process-spawning call. No class C is needed for repr(f), so there is no constructor or unrelated method to introduce. The negative expectation is independently supported by Python call/representation semantics, not a tool outcome.
